snippet.title: Count the Sounds! | Phoneme Song for Kids | Jack Hartmann
snippet.description:
Count the Sounds by Jack Hartmann is a phonemic awareness activity designed to help early learners identify and count individual sounds (phonemes) in words. Through repetition and guided practice, students are encouraged to say words slowly, segment them into their separate sounds, and count each sound using their fingers. The song models correct sound segmentation with simple, age-appropriate words such as cat, ten, jump, at, big, and stop, thereby gradually reinforcing the concept that words are composed of distinct sounds.

By combining listening, speaking, and physical movement (finger counting), the song supports multisensory learning. It strengthens foundational reading skills by helping students map spoken sounds to words, an essential step in decoding and spelling. The playful, structured format promotes concentration, confidence, and engagement while building early literacy skills in a fun and interactive way.

Count the Sounds Lyrics
Use your fingers 1 by 1
Concentrate, learn, and have fun
I'll say a word , then sound it out
You count the sounds, right out loud
Count the sounds in the word cat
/C/ /a/ /t/ again
/C/ /a/ /t/  cat
There are three sounds in the word cat
Count those sounds in the word ten
/ T/ /e/ /n/  again
/T/ /e/ /n/ ten
There are three sounds in the word ten
Count the sounds in the word jump
/J/ /u/ /m//p/ again
/J/ /u/ /m//p/ jump
There are 4 sounds in the word jump
 Use your fingers 1 by 1
Concentrate, learn, and have fun
I'll say a word , Then sound it out
You count the sounds, right out loud
Count those sounds in the word at
/ A/ /t/   again
/A/ /t/ at
There are two sounds in the word at
Count the sounds in the word big
/B/ /i/ /g/ again
/B/ /i/ /g/  big
There are 3 sounds in the word big
Count the sounds in the word stop
/s/ /t/ /o//p/ again
/s/ /t/ /o//p/ stop

snippet.title: The Massive Machine Hidden Under Antarctica
snippet.description:
At the bottom of the earth there’s a massive machine that’s unlike anything you’ve ever seen. That’s because it’s mostly buried under the ice and it’s not looking at the stars… It’s hunting ghosts! 

Specifically, “ghost particles” known as neutrinos. These mysterious particles come from somewhere in space and are smaller than an electron. 

We can only spot them when one accidentally bumps into an atom and that rarely happens so scientists around the world have built massive “telescopes” like this one to try and catch them as they pass – giving us a new way to map the universe.

snippet.title: Dripleaf secret use
snippet.description:
Big dripleaf has a secret use in Minecraft. You probably know that you can easily find lush caves if you mine directly underneath an azalea tree, but you might not know that these lush caves are really useful because of the big dripleaf. Dripleaf is a weird block, because you can stand on it like a normal block, but only for one second, because then it tilts down and becomes non solid. But you can power dripleaf to make them always solid, which means you can make a pathway with one unpowered dripleaf which leads to a secret entrance.
